translation_direction: ja → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Japanese electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Botchan’s brisk, quarrelsome, comic narration is rendered in short punchy sentences with Edokko bluntness, without a regional Vietnamese dialect.
decisions.rationale: The novel’s comedy depends on the speaker’s directness.

decisions.decision: The なもし/菜飯 pun and the 勘五郎 callback are re-created in Vietnamese; sen and rin keep the period money.
decisions.rationale: Jokes must still land for a Vietnamese reader.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘nothing is more reliable than people’ inverted 人間ほどあてにならないものはない; corrected, with Madonna as the referent of あの顔.
Direction of travel fixed (rời Tokyo; xuống tỉnh lẻ); 428, 473 and 479 corrected.
bà Kiyo restored in narration; Hotta’s tớ/cậu and the landlady’s thầy made consistent across parts.
The returned money is the raise; 免職 now a dismissal; 一席伺わせる and 二間 corrected.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: Botchan’s nicknames for the head teacher, Hotta, Noda, Koga and the headmaster, fixed through the novel.

glossary.rationale: Kiyo’s affectionate address for the young master; the old servant is always bà Kiyo in narration.

glossary.rationale: Botchan’s blunt Edokko voice without regional dialect.

glossary.source_term: 天麩羅 / 蕎麦 / 団子
glossary.rationale: Dish names kept as loanwords for the blackboard jokes.

witness_decision: Selected the Aozora Bunko transcription (card 752, file 752_14964, new characters and new kana) of 坊っちゃん, first published in ホトトギス (April 1906); the transcription follows the Chikuma Nihon Bungaku Zenshū edition (筑摩書房, 1st printing 1992-01-20, 2nd printing used for proofreading 1998-03-15; parent text 夏目漱石全集2, ちくま文庫, 1987). Not collated with the 1906 magazine text. Input by 真先芳秋, proofreading by 柳沢成雄; file published 1999-09-13, revised 2011-05-20.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The なもし/菜飯 pun is localised with a modern dish; a period-neutral dish could be considered.

title_review.rationale: Botchan is the established Vietnamese title; the Japanese 坊っちゃん means a young master or spoiled boy and is explained in the introduction.
